column2: it assumes the flavor is not a GSS

column1: However
column2: if this XDR encoding logic is given a legitimate GSS

column1: pseudoflavor but the RPC layer says it does not support that

column2: then the server leaks GSS pseudoflavor

column1: numbers onto the wire.
I confirmed this happens by blacklisting rpcsec_gss_krb5
attempted a client transition from the pseudo-fs to a Kerberos-only
share.  The client received a flavor list containing the Kerberos
pseudoflavor numbers
The encoder logic can check that each pseudoflavor in flavs[] is
less than MAXFLAVOR before writing it into the buffer
this.  But after ""nflavs"" is written into the XDR buffer
encoder can't skip writing flavor information into the buffer when
it discovers the RPC layer doesn't support that flavor.
So count the number of valid flavors as they are written into the
XDR buffer
column2: then write that count into a placeholder in the XDR

column1: buffer when all recognized flavors have been encoded.
